breakdown_notes: Paper: Angrist & Krueger (1991), 'Does Compulsory School Attendance Affect Schooling and Earnings?' (QJE Vol. CVI, Issue 4). This is a 1991 labor-economics paper whose entire empirical content is OLS and two-stage-least-squares (TSLS) regressions on U.S. decennial Census microdata (quarter-of-birth as an instrument for education). The paper reports NO hardware, wall-clock time, API cost, or GPU information — such details are absent from 1991 econometrics papers and none were found in the text or appendix. Falling back to the replication plan: the entire replication is a line-for-line port of the shipped Stata .do files and a SAS reader into R (Stata/SAS are not installed), run on the NEW7080.dta Census extract. The full dataset is a single 19MB Stata file (~1.06M rows, 27 columns; confirmed on disk at /workspace/repo/NEW7080/NEW7080.dta). Per-table subsamples are ~247,199 (1970 Census, born 1920-29), ~329,509 (1980, born 1930-39), and ~486,926 (1980, born 1940-49). The largest model is a TSLS with 30 quarter-by-year interaction instruments on ~487k rows — trivial for CPU; the plan itself notes 'these regressions are modest in size (<=1.06M rows, <=30 instruments) and run fine on CPU; no GPU is required.' There are 7 executable steps (steps 1-7); step 1 is pure setup and steps 2-7 fit regressions / compute group means and detrended series. No step involves model training in the deep-learning sense, no step calls any external LLM API, and no step requires GPU. Each Rscript invocation should complete in seconds to at most a couple of minutes (data load dominates); the whole replication runs well under 5 minutes on a single CPU core, with steps trivially parallelizable across the independent table scripts. Reproducing the full paper additionally requires 1960/1970/1980 enrollment micro-data for Table II (claims C3, C9, C10), which is NOT shipped and is out of scope here — but even that would be CPU-only tabulation, not a compute concern.
dataset_size: ~19 MB Stata file (NEW7080.dta), ~1.06M rows x 27 columns; per-table subsamples 247k-487k rows
estimated_wall_clock: under 5 minutes on a single CPU core
notes_on_repeated_steps: Steps 2-4 apply the same eight-specification OLS/TSLS template to three disjoint Census subsamples (Tables IV/V/VI); step 5 (Table III Wald) and steps 6-7 (Table I education outcomes and Figure I/II/IV/V descriptive series) are additional CPU-only regressions and cell-mean computations on the same data. No seeds/Monte-Carlo repetition; regressions are deterministic closed-form estimates.
